(m): g : fp-lie: No.A-2451 With intent to avoid delay in judicial proceeding due to non-availability of parties, counsels, witncsscs and accused, there is an urgcnt need for a user-fricndly video confcrencing facility and othcr modes of audio-visual electronic linkage for the purposc of hearing of thc cases as well as recording of evidence of witncsses unable to attend.the Court. The information technology is a good tool for spccdy trial and specdy justice. The vidco confercncing will bc an intcgratcd web technology capable of running scamlcssly ovcr Intcrnct/Intranet, Virtual Private Network (VPN) of witness, accuscd and other stakcholders. Thcrcforc, in cxercisc of the powcrs, conferred by Article 227 of thc Constitution of India, rcad with Section 122 of thc Code of Civil Procedurc, 1908 (5 of 1908), Section 23 of thc Madhya Pradesh Civil Courts Act, 1958 and Scction 477 of the Codc of Criininal Proccdure, 1973 (2 of 1974), thc High Court of Madhya Pradesh hcreby, makes the following rules regulating practicc and proccdurc pcrtaining to usc of vidco conferencing for District Courts of Madhya Pradesh, namely:- RULES Chapter I Preliminary
1. Short title, Application and Commenccment.-
(i) Thesc Rules shall be callcd the "The District Courts of Madhya Pradcsh Vidco Conferencing and Audio-Visual Electronic Linkagc Rules, 2020". I 4 (T)] 202020 1601
(ii) Thcy shall apply to Courts.
(iii) Thcy shall come into force from the date of their notification in the Official Gazctte.
2. Definitions.-
(1) In thcsc Rules, unless the contcxt othcrwisc rcquircs ,-
(a) "Advocate" mcans and include an advocate entcred in any roll maintaincd under the provisions of the Advocates Act, 196l and shall also include government pleaders and officers of the department of public prosccution;
(b) "Commissioner" means a person appointed as commissioncr under. thc provisions of Code of Civil Proccdure, 1908 (5 of 1908), or thc Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or any other law for the time being in force;
(c) "Coordinator" means a person nominated as coordinator under Rule 5;
(d) "Court" means Civil Courts established under Civil Courts Act,1958, Criminal Courts as defined in Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (other than Court of Executive Magistrate), any other Special Courts cstablished under any Special Act, Family Courts, Juvenile Justice Board(s) in the State of Madhya Pradesh and shall includes a physical court and a virtual court or tribunal;
(e) "Court Point" means the courtroom or one or more places where the court is physically convencd, or the place where a commissioner or an inquiring officer holds proceedings pursuant to thc directions of the court;
(f) "Court Room" means the place or room or enclosed space in which court of law is held in front of the judgc(s);
(g) "Court User" means a user participating in court proceedings through video conferencing at a court point and includcs presiding judge of court;
(h) "Designated Video Conferencing software' means a software approved by the High Court for thc use of video confercncing;
(i)· "Electronic records" shall bear the same meaning as assigned under the Information Technology Act, 2000; () "Exceptional circumstances' includes a pandemic, natural calamities, circumstances affccting law and order where it is expcdicnt for effective administration of justice and any other matter relating to the safety of the advocatcs, accuscd persons, witnesses or any other required to be present before the court and includes any such incident or circumstances which may be declared to be an "exceptional circumstance" by the court; 1602 202020 [TT 4 (T)
(k) "Live Link' means and includes a live television link, audio-video electronic means or othcr arrangcments whereby a witness, an accuscd, party, pleader, advocate (s) or any other person required by court to remain present in the court while physically abscnt from the courtroom is neverthcless virtually present in the courtroom by remote communication using technology to give evidencc and be cross-examined or to present arguments or assist the Court or for any other purpose in a judicial proceeding;
(1) "Institutional Remote Point' means the courtroom or one or more places in the court complex where the remote point is physically convcned for facilitating the audio-visual electronic linkagc with courts points;
(m) "Remote Point" is a place where any person or persons are requircd to be present or appcar through a video link;
(n) "Remote User' means a user participating in court proceedings through video conferencing at a remote point.
(o) "Required Person" includes :
(i) the person who is to be examined as a witness or otherwise; or
(ii) person in whosc prescnce certain proceedings are to be recorded or conductcd; or
(imi) an advocatc or a party in pcrson who intends to examine a witness; or
(iv) any person who is requircd to make submissions before the court; or
(v) any othcr person who is permitted by the court to appear through video conferencing or other modes of audio visual electronic linkage;
(p) "Rules" shall mcan these rulcs and any referencc to a rule, sub-rulc or schedule shall be a refcrence to a rulc, sub-rulc or schcdule of thesc rulcs;
(q) "Video conferencing" means and includes to conduct a confercncc betwcen two or morc participants at different sites by using computer networks to transmit audio and video data.
(2) The words and phrases used but not defincd hercin shall bear the samc mcaning as assigncd to thcm in M.P. Civil Court Rules, 196l; Rules and Ordcrs (Criminal); Codc of Civil Procedure, 1908, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Information Tcchnology Act, 2000 and the General Clauses Act, 1897. 3. General Principles Governing Video Conferencing and other modes of audio-visual electronic linkagc.-
(a) Vidco confercncing and othcr modes of audio-visual clcctronic linkage facility may bc used at all stagcs of judicial proceedings and proccedings conducted by the court, where a person is required to be prescnt or appear is located intrastate; intcrstate or overseas.
(b) All procecdings conducted by a Court by way of video conferencing andothermodes of audio-visualelectroniclinkageshall bejudicial procecdings and all the courtesies and protocols applicablc to a physical court shall apply to these virtual proceedings. The protocol provided in Schedule I shall be adhered to 0forproceedings conducted by way of video conferencing and other modes of audiovisual electronic linkage.
(c) All relevant statutory provisions applicable to judicial proceedings including, but not limited to provisions of the M.P. Civil Court Rules, 1961; Rules and Orders (Criminal); Code of Civil Proccdurc, 1908 (hereinafter it will be called "C.P.C.") Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter it will be called "Cr.P.C.") Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (abbreviated hereafter as the Evidcnce Act) and Information ‘Technology Act, 200o(abbreviatedhercafteras sthc I'T Act), shall apply‘to proceedings conducted by video conferencing and other modes of audio-visual electronic linkage.
(d) Subject to maintaining indepcndence, impartiality and credibility of judicial proccedings and subjcct to such dircctions as the Chief Justice may issue, courts may adopt such technological advanccs as may become available from time to timc for ensuring propcr conduction of proccedings through video conferencing and other modes of audio-visual clectronic linkage.
(e) The rules as applicable to a court shall mutatis mutandis apply to a commissioner appointed by the court to record evidence and to an inquiry officcr conducting an inquiry.
(f) Unless cxpressly permitted, no person or entity, either at Court Point or at Institutional Remotc Point or at Remotc Point, shall bc permitted to record the proceedings conducted by video conferencing or other modes of audio-visual electronic linkage. In case of violation it will be punishable in accordance with law.
(g) The person defined in rulc 2 (1)(o) shall provide identity proof as recognised by the Government of India/State Government /Union Territory to thc court point coordinator via personal email. In case identity proof is not readily available the person concerned shall furnish the following personal details: namc, parcntagc and permanent address, temporary address if any and will make available as per direction of the court, however the court may, upon satisfaction allow such person to participate in proceedings without production of identity proof. 1604 202020 [I 4 ()
4. Facilities recommend for Video Conferencing.- The following cquipment is recommended for conducting proceedings by video confcrencing at the Court Point and at the Institutional Remote Point:
(i) desktop laptop, mobile devices with uninterrupted internet connectivity and printer;
(ii) device cnsuring uninterrupted power supply;
(iii) vidco Camera;
(iv) microphoncs and speakers;
(v) display unit;
(vi) documcnt visualizer;
(vii) provision of a fircwall;
(viii) adcquatc scating arrangcments ensuring privacy;
(ix) adcquatcd lighting;
(x) availability of a quiet and secure space;
(xi) scanner including mobile scanner.
5. Preparatory Arrangements.-
(1) Therc shall be a Coordinator both at the Court Point and at thc institutional Rcmote Point from which any required person is to be cxamined or heard or is directcd to remain prescnt. Howevcr, coordinator may be rcquircd at the remote point only whcn a witness or a person accused of an offence is to be examincd.
(2) In all civil and criminal courts, the persons nominated by the High Court or the concerncd District Judge within whose jurisdiction thc rcspective civil or criminal court is present, shall perform thc functions of thc coordinators at the Court Point as well as the Rcmotc Point as provided in sub-rule (3)

(4) When a Required person is at any of the Remote Points mentioncd in sub rules (3) and vidco confcrcncing facilitics arc not available at any of thcsc places the concerned court may formally request thc Principal District Judge, in whosc jurisdiction the Remote Point is situated to appoint a coordinator for and to provide a vidco confercncing facility from proximate place and suitable court premises.
(5) The coordinators at both Court Points and Institutional Remote Points shall ensure that rcquiremcnts set out in Rulc 4 are complicd with, so that the proceedings are conductcd seamlessly.
(6) Thc coordinator at the Rcmote the Point shall cnsure that;
(a) all advocatcs and/or requircd persons scheduled to appcar in a particular procecding are ready at the Remote Point designated for video conferencing at least 30 minutes before thc schcduled time;
(b) no unauthorised recording device is used;
(c) no unauthoriscd person cntcrs thc video conference room when thc vidco confcrcnce is in progress;
(d) thc pcrson being cxamined is not prompted, tutored, coaxcd, induccd or coerced in any manner by any person and that thc pcrson bcing examined does not refer to any document, script or device without the permission of the court concerned during the course of examination.
(7) Where the witncss to be examined through video conferencing requires or if it is othcrwise expcdient to do so, the Court shall givc sufficient notice in advancc, setting out the schedule of vidco confercncing and in appropriate cases may transmit non-editablc digital scanncd copics of all or any part of the coordinator of thc conccrncd Rcmote Point designatcd in accordance with sub-rule (3).
(8) Bcforc thc schedule video conferencing date, the coordinator at the Court point shall. ensure that the coordinator at the Institutional 4(π)] 202020 1607 Remote Point or Remote Point receives certified copics, printouts or a soft copy of the non-editable scanned copies of all or any part of the record of proceedings which may be requircd for recording statements or evidence, or for reference. However, these shall be permitted to bc used by the Required Person only with the permission of the court.
(9) Where Required person is connected from a place which is not a Remote Point, or where no coordinator is available at Remote Point, court shall ensure that Required Person receives all copies as mentioned in preceding rule.
(10) Whenever required the court shall order the coordinator at the Remote Point or at the Court Point to provide-
(a) a translator in case the person to be examined is not conversant with the official language of the court;
(b) an expert in sign languages in case the person to be examined is impaired in speech and/or hearing;
(c) an interpreter or a special cducator, as thc case may be, in case a person to be examined is diffcrently abled, either temporarily or permanently;
(d) a person for rcading of documents in case the person to be examined is visually challenged. Chapter III Procedure for Video Conferencing
6. Application for Appearance, Evidence and Submission by Video Conferencing.-
(1) Any party to the procccding or witness, save and except where proceedings are initiated at the instance of the court or public prosecutor, may move a request for video conferencing. A party or witness seeking a video conferencing proceeding shall do so by making a request in the form prescribed in schedule Il.
(2) In the civil cases, any proposal to move a request to for vidco conferencing should first be discussed with the other party or parties to the proceeding, except where not possible or inappropriate, for example in cases such as urgent applications. However the court may, as its discretion, initiate process for hearing or any case through video conferencing and other modes of audio-visual electronic linkage. 1608 202020 [ 4 (T)
(3) On receipt of such a request and upon hearing all concerned persons the court will pass an appropriatc order after ascertaining that the application is not filed with an intention to impede a fair trial or to delay the proccedings.
(4) While allowing a request for video conferencing the Court may also fix the schcdule for convening the video conferencing.
(5) In case the video conferencing event is convened for making oral submissions, the order may require the advocate or party in person to submit written arguments and prccedents, if any, in advance on the official email ID of the court concerncd.
(6) Costs, if directed to bc paid, shall be deposited within the prescribed timc, commcncing from thc date on which the order convening proceedings through vidco conferencing is received.
7. Servicc of Summons.- Summons issued to a witness who is to be examined through video conferencing, shall mention the date, time and venue of the concerncd Rcmote Point and shall dircct the witness to attend in person along with proof of identity or an affidavit to that effcct. Such summons may be servcd through clcctronic mcans. Howevcr, the existing rules regarding servicc of summons and the conscquenccs for non-attendancc, as provided in the C.P.C. and Cr.P.C. shall apply with respect to service of summons for proceedings conducted by video conferencing.
8. Examination of persons through video conferencing and other modes of audio-visual electronic linkagc.-
(1) Any pcrson bcing examined, including a witness shall before bcing examined through video confcrencing, produce and submit proof of idcntity by submitting and idcntity document issued or duly recognizcd by thc Govcrnmcnt of India, Statc Government, Union Territory, or in the abscnce of such a document, an affidavit attested by any of thc authorities refcrred to in section 139 of the C.P.C. or section 297 of the Cr.P.C. as the case may be. The affidavit will inter alia state that thc person who is shown to be the party to the proceedings or as a witncss, is the same person, who is to dcpose at the virtual hcaring. A copy of thc proof of identity or affidavit, as the case may be, will be madc availablc to thc oppositc party:
Provided that in absence of identity proof as required in subrule (1) the identity of thc person required to be present or appear shall be confirmcd by the court with the assistance of the co-ordinator at remote point at the time of proceedings through video conferencing. HTI 4 (T)] 202020 1609
(2) The person being examined will ordinarily be examined during the working hours of the court concerned or at such time as the court may deem fit. The oath will be administered to the person being examined by the coordinator at the Court Point. 3 Where the person being examined or accused to be presented is in custody, the statement or, as the case may be, the testimony may be recorded through video conferencing. The court shall provide adequate opportunity to the under-trial prisoner to consult with their counsel before and after the video conferencing. 4 Subject to the provisions for examination of witnesses contained in the Evidcnce Act, beforc the examination of the witness, the documents, if any, sought to be relied upon shall be transmitted by the applicant to the witness so that the witncss acquires familiarity with the said documents. The applicant will submit an acknowledgement with the court in this behalf. 5） If a person is examined with reference to a particular document then the summon to witness must be accompanied by a duly certified photocopy of the document. The original document should be exhibited at the Court Point in accordance with the deposition of the concerned person being examined.
(6) The court would be at liberty to record the demeanour of the person being examined. The court will note the objections raiscd during the deposition of the person being examined and rule on them.
(8) The Court shall obtain the signature of thc person being examincd on the transcript once the examination is concluded. The signcd transcript will form part of the record of the judicial proceedings. The signature on the-transcript of the person being examined shall be obtained in either of the following ways.-
(a) If digital signatures are available at both the concerned Court Point and Remote Point, the soft copy of the transcript digitally signed by the presiding judge at the Court Point shall be scnt by the official email to the Remote Point.where a print out of the same will be taken and signed by the person bcing cxamincd. A scanned copy of the transcript d digitally y signed by the coordinator at the Rcmote Point would be transmitted by official email of thc Court Point. The hard copy of the signed transcript will be dispatched after the testimony is over, preferably within three days by the coordinator at the Remote Point to the Court Point by recognised courier/registered $1610 202020 [HTI 4 () speed post.
(b) If digital signatures are not available, the printout of the transcript shall be signed by the prcsiding Judge and the representative of the partics, if any, at the Court Point and shall be sent in non-cditable scanncd format to the official cmail account of the remote point where a printout of the same will be taken and signed by the person examined and countersigncd by the Coordinator at the Remote Point. A non-editable scanncd format of the transcript so signcd shall be sent by the Coordinator of the Remote Point to the official cmail account of the Court Point where a print out of the same will be takcn and shall be madc a part of the judicial record. The hard copy would also be dispatched prcferably within three days by thc Coordinator at the Remote Point to the Court Point by recognised courier/registered speed post.
(9) An audio-visual recording of the examination of witnesses shall be prepared at the Court point. An encrypted master copy with hash value shall bc retaincd as a part of the record.
(10) The court may, at the rcquest of a person to be examined, or on its own motion, taking into account the best interest of the person to bc examined, dircct appropriate measures to protect the privacy of thc person examined bearing in mind aspects such as age, gender, physical condition and recognized customs and practices.
(11) The coordinator at the Rcmote Point shall ensure that no person is present at the Remote Point, save and exccpt the person bcing examined and thosc whose presence is decmed administrativcly nccessary by the coordinator for the proceedings to continue.
(12) The court may also impose such othcr conditions as arc neccssary in a givcn set of facts for effcctive rccording of evidence (especially to ensure compliance with rule 5 (6) (d).
